en: We are planning a small get-together at home on Saturday.
tamil: சனிக்கிழமை வீட்டுல ஒரு சின்ன கூடுகை பண்ண பிளான் பண்றோம்.
context: Telling a friend about your weekend plan.
explain: 'Are planning' shows a plan already being made for the near future.
usage: Use it when you tell friends or relatives about a plan you are making.
leelaQ: What are you planning for this Saturday?
answer: I am planning to relax at home with my family.

en: I will join you for lunch tomorrow.
tamil: நாளைக்கு மதிய சாப்பாட்டுக்கு நானும் உங்களோட சேர்ந்துக்கறேன்.
context: Accepting a colleague's lunch invitation.
explain: 'Will' is used for a decision made at the moment of speaking.
usage: Say it to a colleague when you accept an invitation to eat together.
leelaQ: Would you like to have lunch with me tomorrow?
answer: Yes, I will join you for lunch tomorrow.

en: Thank you for inviting me to your cousin's wedding.
tamil: உங்க cousin கல்யாணத்துக்கு கூப்பிட்டதுக்கு நன்றி.
context: Thanking someone for a wedding invitation.
explain: 'Thank you for' is followed by an -ing word to give the reason for thanks.
usage: Say it to a host when you receive an invitation to a function.
leelaQ: How do you thank someone who invites you to a wedding?
answer: I say thank you for inviting me and promise to come.

en: I am sorry, I can't come to the party this evening.
tamil: மன்னிக்கணும், இன்னைக்கு சாயங்காலம் பார்ட்டிக்கு வர முடியாது.
context: Politely declining a party invitation.
explain: 'Can't' shows you are not able to do something. Starting with 'I am sorry' is polite.
usage: Use it to refuse an invitation politely without hurting the host.
leelaQ: Why might you refuse a party invitation?
answer: I might refuse because I have to finish some work.

en: We are going to visit my grandmother in Madurai this Diwali.
tamil: இந்த தீபாவளிக்கு மதுரையில இருக்கற பாட்டியைப் பார்க்கப் போறோம்.
context: Sharing your festival travel plan.
explain: 'Are going to' talks about a plan you have already decided.
usage: Use it when colleagues or friends ask where you will spend the festival.
leelaQ: Where will you spend the next festival?
answer: We are going to celebrate it at my native place.

en: Let's meet at the bus stand at six o'clock.
tamil: ஆறு மணிக்கு பஸ் ஸ்டாண்டில் சந்திக்கலாம்.
context: Fixing a meeting time with a friend.
explain: 'Let's' is used to suggest something we do together.
usage: Say it when you finalise the time and place with a friend.
leelaQ: Where do you usually meet your friends?
answer: We usually meet near the tea shop in our street.

en: I have already made plans for Sunday.
tamil: ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமைக்கு நான் ஏற்கனவே பிளான் பண்ணிட்டேன்.
context: Saying you are busy on Sunday.
explain: 'Have made' shows the plan is already done before now. 'Already' stresses this.
usage: Use it to refuse a new invitation because you have something else fixed.
leelaQ: Are you free on Sunday?
answer: No, I have already made plans for Sunday.

en: The meeting has been moved to Thursday afternoon.
tamil: மீட்டிங்கை வியாழன் மதியத்துக்கு மாத்திட்டாங்க.
context: Informing your team about a new meeting day.
explain: 'Has been moved' is passive. It tells the result without saying who moved it.
usage: Use it at work to tell people about a changed schedule.
leelaQ: How do you inform your team about a changed meeting?
answer: I send a short message with the new day and time.

en: I'll check my calendar and let you know.
tamil: என் calendar பார்த்துட்டு சொல்றேன்.
context: Replying to an invitation when you are not sure.
explain: 'Let you know' means to tell you later. It is a safe way to delay a reply.
usage: Use it when you cannot say yes or no immediately.
leelaQ: What do you say when you are not sure about a plan?
answer: I say I will check my calendar and tell them later.

en: We went to a movie last Friday and had dinner outside.
tamil: போன வெள்ளிக்கிழமை படத்துக்குப் போய் வெளியில சாப்பிட்டோம்.
context: Telling a friend about your last weekend.
explain: 'Went' and 'had' are past forms. 'Last Friday' shows when it happened.
usage: Use it to share your weekend activities with friends at work.
leelaQ: What did you do last Friday?
answer: I watched a movie and ate dinner with my friends.

en: My parents are coming to stay with us next week.
tamil: அடுத்த வாரம் அம்மா அப்பா எங்க கூட தங்க வராங்க.
context: Telling a friend about family guests.
explain: Present continuous with 'next week' shows a fixed arrangement.
usage: Use it to explain why you will be busy or away from other plans.
leelaQ: Who is coming to your house next week?
answer: My uncle and aunt are coming to our house.

en: I would love to come, but I have an exam on Monday.
tamil: வர ரொம்ப ஆசைதான், ஆனா திங்கட்கிழமை பரீட்சை இருக்கு.
context: A student declining an outing.
explain: 'Would love to' is warm. 'But' then gives the reason for saying no.
usage: Use it to decline kindly while giving a clear reason.
leelaQ: How do you refuse an invitation kindly?
answer: I say I would love to come but I have other work.

en: We will celebrate her birthday on the terrace.
tamil: அவ பிறந்தநாளை மொட்டை மாடியில கொண்டாடுவோம்.
context: Planning a birthday surprise with family.
explain: 'Will celebrate' states a plan. 'On the terrace' says where.
usage: Use it when you plan a family celebration with others.
leelaQ: How will you celebrate your next birthday?
answer: I will celebrate it with cake and my close friends.

en: I usually go to the temple on Sunday mornings.
tamil: நான் பொதுவா ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை காலையில கோயிலுக்குப் போவேன்.
context: Describing your weekly routine to a new friend.
explain: 'Usually' goes before the main verb to show a regular habit.
usage: Use it to explain your weekend habits to someone new.
leelaQ: What do you usually do on Sunday morning?
answer: I usually clean the house and then go to the temple.

en: The train leaves at ten, so we should reach the station early.
tamil: ரயில் பத்து மணிக்குக் கிளம்பும், அதனால சீக்கிரமே ஸ்டேஷனுக்குப் போகணும்.
context: Planning a train trip with your family.
explain: 'So' joins a reason with a result. 'Should' gives advice.
usage: Use it when you plan travel timing with family or friends.
leelaQ: How early do you reach the station for a train?
answer: I reach the station about thirty minutes early.

en: Our family trip to Ooty is confirmed for December.
tamil: டிசம்பர்ல ஊட்டிக்கு எங்க குடும்ப டிரிப் உறுதியாயிடுச்சு.
context: Sharing a confirmed holiday plan.
explain: 'Is confirmed' means the plan is final and sure.
usage: Use it to tell friends that a holiday plan is now final.
leelaQ: Which place do you want to visit on a holiday?
answer: I want to visit the hills with my family.

en: I'm free after five, so we can talk then.
tamil: ஐந்து மணிக்கு மேல ஃப்ரீ தான், அப்போ பேசலாம்.
context: Suggesting a time to a colleague.
explain: 'Free' here means not busy. 'So' links the time with the suggestion.
usage: Use it to offer a time when someone wants to discuss something.
leelaQ: When are you free to talk in the evening?
answer: I am free after seven when I come home.

en: We have booked the tickets for the 15th.
tamil: பதினைந்தாம் தேதிக்கு டிக்கெட் புக் பண்ணிட்டோம்.
context: Telling relatives that travel is booked.
explain: 'Have booked' shows a finished action that matters now.
usage: Use it to tell family that the travel tickets are ready.
leelaQ: Have you ever booked tickets for a family trip?
answer: Yes, I booked train tickets for our trip to Chennai.

en: I am going to start going to the gym from next Monday.
tamil: அடுத்த திங்கட்கிழமையிலிருந்து ஜிம்முக்குப் போகப் போறேன்.
context: Sharing a new routine plan.
explain: 'From next Monday' tells the starting point of a new plan.
usage: Use it when you tell friends about a new habit you plan to start.
leelaQ: What new habit do you want to start?
answer: I want to start walking every morning from Monday.

en: We will have a long weekend because of the holiday.
tamil: விடுமுறை வர்றதால நமக்கு நீண்ட வார இறுதி கிடைக்கும்.
context: Talking about a coming holiday at office.
explain: 'Because of' is followed by a noun. 'Long weekend' means three or more days off.
usage: Use it at work when a holiday joins the weekend.
leelaQ: What do you do on a long weekend?
answer: I go to my hometown and meet my relatives.

en: She has invited the whole family for lunch on Sunday.
tamil: ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை மதிய சாப்பாட்டுக்கு அவ முழு குடும்பத்தையும் கூப்பிட்டிருக்கா.
context: Telling your mother about an invitation.
explain: 'Has invited' shows an invitation that is still open.
usage: Use it to pass on an invitation to someone in your family.
leelaQ: Who invited you to a function recently?
answer: My neighbour invited us to her housewarming.

en: I will call you once I reach home.
tamil: வீட்டுக்குப் போனவுடனே உங்களுக்கு போன் பண்றேன்.
context: Promising to call after reaching home.
explain: 'Once' means as soon as. The time part uses the present tense, not 'will'.
usage: Use it when you promise to contact a friend later.
leelaQ: What do you tell your family when you travel alone?
answer: I tell them I will call once I reach safely.

en: Our school reunion is on the last Saturday of this month.
tamil: எங்க பள்ளி நண்பர்கள் சந்திப்பு இந்த மாசம் கடைசி சனிக்கிழமை.
context: Talking about a reunion date.
explain: Present simple is used for fixed events on a calendar.
usage: Use it to tell people the date of a scheduled event.
leelaQ: Do you meet your old school friends often?
answer: Yes, we meet once a year at a reunion.

en: We were planning to go out, but it started raining.
tamil: வெளியில போக பிளான் பண்ணிட்டு இருந்தோம், ஆனா மழை பெய்ய ஆரம்பிச்சுது.
context: Explaining why a plan failed.
explain: 'Were planning to' shows a plan that did not happen. 'But' shows the problem.
usage: Use it to explain why you cancelled an outing.
leelaQ: What do you do when rain spoils your plan?
answer: I stay at home and watch a movie with my family.

en: Let me know if you can make it on Friday.
tamil: வெள்ளிக்கிழமை வர முடியுமான்னு சொல்லுங்க.
context: Asking a friend to confirm attendance.
explain: 'Make it' means to be able to attend. 'Let me know' is a friendly request.
usage: Use it after you invite someone and need their reply.
leelaQ: How do you ask a friend to confirm a plan?
answer: I send a message and ask them to let me know.

en: I'm meeting my college friends at the beach this evening.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு சாயங்காலம் பீச்சுல என் காலேஜ் ஃப்ரெண்ட்ஸைப் பார்க்கப் போறேன்.
context: Telling a colleague your evening plan.
explain: Present continuous with a time word shows a fixed plan for today.
usage: Use it when someone asks what you are doing after office.
leelaQ: What are you doing this evening?
answer: I am meeting a friend for tea near my office.

en: We will be travelling next Tuesday, so I will be on leave.
tamil: அடுத்த செவ்வாய்க்கிழமை பயணம் இருக்கு, அதனால நான் லீவுல இருப்பேன்.
context: Informing your manager of planned leave.
explain: 'Will be on leave' means you will be absent from work.
usage: Use it to tell a manager or team why you will be away.
leelaQ: How do you inform your office about leave?
answer: I send an email to my manager a week before.

en: The function starts at nine, but we should reach by eight.
tamil: விசேஷம் ஒன்பது மணிக்குத்தான், ஆனா நாம எட்டு மணிக்குள்ள போகணும்.
context: Planning to arrive early for a function.
explain: 'Should' gives advice. 'By eight' means not later than eight.
usage: Use it when you plan the timing for a family function.
leelaQ: How early do you reach a family function?
answer: I reach early to help my relatives with the work.

en: My friend has asked me to go trekking next month.
tamil: என் நண்பன் அடுத்த மாசம் டிரெக்கிங் போகக் கூப்பிட்டிருக்கான்.
context: Sharing an invitation with family.
explain: 'Has asked me to' is followed by the base verb.
usage: Use it to tell your family about an invitation and ask their view.
leelaQ: Would you like to go trekking?
answer: Yes, I would love to go trekking with my friends.

en: I was thinking of visiting the new mall this weekend.
tamil: இந்த வார இறுதியில புது மால் போகலாம்னு யோசிச்சிட்டு இருந்தேன்.
context: Suggesting an idea in a soft way.
explain: 'Was thinking of' makes a suggestion sound soft and open.
usage: Use it to suggest a plan gently to a friend or family member.
leelaQ: Where were you thinking of going this weekend?
answer: I was thinking of going to the park.

en: We'll decide the dates after talking to everyone.
tamil: எல்லார்கிட்டயும் பேசின பிறகு தேதியை முடிவு பண்ணுவோம்.
context: Planning a group trip.
explain: 'After talking' uses an -ing form after 'after'.
usage: Use it when a group plan is not final yet.
leelaQ: How does your group decide a trip date?
answer: We ask everyone and choose a date that suits all.

en: I will be out of town from the 20th to the 25th.
tamil: நான் இருபதாம் தேதி முதல் இருபத்தைந்து வரை ஊர்ல இருக்க மாட்டேன்.
context: Telling a client about your absence.
explain: 'From ... to ...' gives the start and end of a period.
usage: Use it to tell clients or friends you are not available for some days.
leelaQ: When will you be out of town next?
answer: I will be out of town during the Pongal holidays.

en: Everyone is excited about the picnic on Sunday.
tamil: ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை சுற்றுலாவுக்கு எல்லாரும் ரொம்ப உற்சாகமா இருக்காங்க.
context: Describing the mood before a picnic.
explain: 'Excited about' is followed by a noun. It shows happy waiting.
usage: Use it to talk about a group plan with your friends.
leelaQ: Are you excited about any plan these days?
answer: Yes, I am excited about my cousin's wedding next month.

en: I'm afraid I have another meeting at that time.
tamil: அந்த நேரத்துல எனக்கு இன்னொரு மீட்டிங் இருக்குன்னு நினைக்கிறேன்.
context: Declining a meeting time politely.
explain: 'I'm afraid' is a polite way to give bad news.
usage: Use it at work to refuse a time because you are busy.
leelaQ: How do you refuse a meeting time politely?
answer: I say I have another meeting and suggest a new time.

en: We had planned a trip, but we postponed it because of exams.
tamil: ஒரு டிரிப் பிளான் பண்ணியிருந்தோம், ஆனா பரீட்சையால தள்ளி வெச்சோம்.
context: Explaining a postponed trip.
explain: 'Had planned' is past perfect: the plan was made before the later event.
usage: Use it to explain why a plan was delayed.
leelaQ: Have you ever postponed a plan? Why?
answer: Yes, I postponed a trip because I fell sick.

en: I'll pick you up from the station at seven.
tamil: ஏழு மணிக்கு ஸ்டேஷன்ல வந்து உன்னைக் கூட்டிட்டுப் போறேன்.
context: Offering to pick up a guest.
explain: 'Pick up' means to collect someone by vehicle.
usage: Use it when a guest or relative is arriving by train or bus.
leelaQ: Who will you pick up from the station?
answer: I will pick up my uncle from the station.

en: Our office party is on the 30th, and families are welcome.
tamil: எங்க ஆபீஸ் பார்ட்டி முப்பதாம் தேதி, குடும்பத்தோட வரலாம்.
context: Inviting a friend to an office event.
explain: 'Welcome' here means allowed and invited.
usage: Use it when you tell someone about an event they can join.
leelaQ: Do you enjoy office parties?
answer: Yes, I enjoy them because I can meet my colleagues.

en: She is hoping to see you at the engagement.
tamil: நிச்சயதார்த்தத்துல உங்களைப் பார்க்கணும்னு அவ எதிர்பார்க்கறா.
context: Passing on a wish to attend.
explain: 'Is hoping to' shows a wish about the future.
usage: Use it to tell someone that the host really wants them to come.
leelaQ: Who do you hope to meet at a function?
answer: I hope to meet my old school friends.

en: I will definitely be there on time.
tamil: நான் கண்டிப்பா சரியான நேரத்துக்கு அங்க இருப்பேன்.
context: Promising to attend a function.
explain: 'Definitely' makes the promise strong. It goes after 'will'.
usage: Use it to assure a host that you will come on time.
leelaQ: How do you promise someone you will come?
answer: I say I will definitely be there on time.

en: We are leaving for Kodaikanal early tomorrow morning.
tamil: நாளைக்கு அதிகாலையில கொடைக்கானலுக்குக் கிளம்பறோம்.
context: Telling a neighbour about your trip.
explain: Present continuous with 'tomorrow' shows an arranged plan.
usage: Use it to tell neighbours why the house will be locked.
leelaQ: What time are you leaving tomorrow?
answer: I am leaving at six in the morning.

en: My brother's engagement was fixed for the second of January.
tamil: என் அண்ணன் நிச்சயதார்த்தம் ஜனவரி இரண்டாம் தேதிக்கு முடிவாகியிருக்கு.
context: Sharing a family event date.
explain: 'Was fixed' is passive past: the date was decided.
usage: Use it to tell friends about a family function date.
leelaQ: What family function is coming soon?
answer: My cousin's wedding is coming next month.

en: I'd rather stay at home this weekend and rest.
tamil: இந்த வார இறுதியில வீட்லயே ஓய்வெடுக்க விரும்பறேன்.
context: Declining outing plans because you are tired.
explain: 'I'd rather' is followed by the base verb and shows preference.
usage: Use it to say politely that you prefer a quiet plan.
leelaQ: Do you prefer staying home or going out?
answer: I would rather stay at home and rest.

en: The dinner is on me this time.
tamil: இந்த தடவை சாப்பாட்டு செலவு என்னோடது.
context: Offering to pay for friends.
explain: 'On me' means I will pay.
usage: Use it when you invite friends and want to pay.
leelaQ: Who pays when you eat with friends?
answer: We share the bill equally.

en: He said he would come, but he didn't turn up.
tamil: வர்றேன்னு சொன்னான், ஆனா வரவே இல்ல.
context: Complaining about a friend who did not come.
explain: 'Turn up' means to arrive. 'Would' is the past form of 'will'.
usage: Use it when someone breaks a promise to come.
leelaQ: What do you do when a friend does not turn up?
answer: I call them and ask what happened.

en: We'll go for a walk after dinner if the weather is good.
tamil: வானிலை நல்லா இருந்தா சாப்பாட்டுக்குப் பிறகு நடக்கப் போவோம்.
context: Making a conditional plan.
explain: The 'if' part uses the present tense, the main part uses 'will'.
usage: Use it to make a plan that depends on something.
leelaQ: What will you do if it rains tomorrow?
answer: I will stay at home and read a book.

en: The house-warming ceremony is next Friday at eight in the morning.
tamil: புதுமனை புகுவிழா அடுத்த வெள்ளிக்கிழமை காலை எட்டு மணிக்கு.
context: Giving details of a function.
explain: Present simple is used for a fixed event. The place of time words matters.
usage: Use it when you give the date and time of a family function.
leelaQ: Have you attended a house-warming ceremony?
answer: Yes, I attended my friend's ceremony last year.

en: I have been looking forward to this holiday for months.
tamil: இந்த விடுமுறைக்காக மாசக்கணக்கா காத்திருக்கேன்.
context: Showing excitement about a trip.
explain: 'Have been looking forward to' is followed by a noun.
usage: Use it to show you are very happy about a coming plan.
leelaQ: What are you looking forward to this year?
answer: I am looking forward to my sister's wedding.

en: We will finish the work by Friday and then relax.
tamil: வெள்ளிக்கிழமைக்குள்ள வேலையை முடிச்சிட்டு ஓய்வெடுப்போம்.
context: Planning with teammates.
explain: 'By Friday' means not later than Friday.
usage: Use it with teammates when you plan to rest after a deadline.
leelaQ: What do you do after finishing a big task?
answer: I take a short rest and meet my friends.

en: I haven't decided yet, but I'll probably say yes.
tamil: இன்னும் முடிவு பண்ணல, ஆனா சரின்னு சொல்லிடுவேன்னு நினைக்கிறேன்.
context: Giving a half answer to an invitation.
explain: 'Haven't decided yet' shows no final decision. 'Probably' shows likely.
usage: Use it when you are leaning towards accepting an invitation.
leelaQ: Do you decide quickly or slowly about plans?
answer: I decide slowly and think about it first.

en: We can't go out tonight because the guests are arriving.
tamil: விருந்தினர்கள் வர்றதால இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரி நம்மால வெளியில போக முடியாது.
context: Explaining why you cannot go out.
explain: 'Can't' shows it is not possible. 'Because' gives the reason.
usage: Use it to explain a refusal to family or friends.
leelaQ: Who comes to your house as guests?
answer: My relatives come during the festivals.

en: I won't be able to attend the class tomorrow.
tamil: நாளைக்கு என்னால வகுப்புக்கு வர முடியாது.
context: Telling a teacher you will miss class.
explain: 'Won't be able to' is a polite way to say you cannot do something later.
usage: Use it to tell a teacher or boss about an absence in advance.
leelaQ: How do you tell a teacher you will miss class?
answer: I send a message and give the reason.

en: Don't worry, I won't forget your birthday party.
tamil: கவலைப்படாதே, உன் பிறந்தநாள் பார்ட்டியை மறக்க மாட்டேன்.
context: Reassuring a friend.
explain: 'Don't worry' calms the listener. 'Won't forget' promises.
usage: Use it when a friend worries you will miss an event.
leelaQ: Do you forget dates easily?
answer: No, I keep all important dates in my phone.

en: We never go out on weekdays because of work.
tamil: வேலை இருக்கறதால நாங்க வார நாட்கள்ல வெளியில போகவே மாட்டோம்.
context: Describing your family routine.
explain: 'Never' goes before the main verb and means not at any time.
usage: Use it to explain your usual routine to friends.
leelaQ: Why do people avoid going out on weekdays?
answer: They are tired after a long day at work.

en: I'm not available on Monday, but Tuesday works for me.
tamil: திங்கட்கிழமை நான் ஃப்ரீ இல்ல, ஆனா செவ்வாய்க்கிழமை சரியா இருக்கும்.
context: Suggesting another day for a meeting.
explain: 'Not available' is a polite way to say you are busy. 'Works for me' means suits me.
usage: Use it at work to suggest another day.
leelaQ: Which day of the week suits you best?
answer: Saturday suits me best because I am free.

en: No problem, we can do it some other day.
tamil: பரவாயில்ல, வேற நாள் பண்ணிக்கலாம்.
context: Accepting a friend's refusal kindly.
explain: 'No problem' is a warm reply. 'Some other day' suggests a new time.
usage: Use it when a friend cannot come and you stay friendly.
leelaQ: What do you say when a friend cancels?
answer: I say no problem and suggest another day.

en: Are you free this Sunday?
tamil: இந்த ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை ஃப்ரீயா இருக்கீங்களா?
context: Checking a friend's availability.
explain: 'Free' here means not busy. This is a common opening before an invitation.
usage: Use it before you invite someone, to check their time.
leelaQ: Are you free on Sundays?
answer: Yes, I am usually free on Sunday afternoons.

en: Would you like to join us for dinner tonight?
tamil: இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரி எங்களோட சாப்பிட வர்றீங்களா?
context: Inviting a colleague to dinner.
explain: 'Would you like to' is a polite way to invite someone.
usage: Use it to invite someone politely at work or at home.
leelaQ: Who would you like to invite for dinner?
answer: I would like to invite my best friend.

en: What time shall we start from home tomorrow?
tamil: நாளைக்கு எத்தனை மணிக்கு வீட்டுலருந்து கிளம்பலாம்?
context: Fixing the time with a friend.
explain: 'Shall we' is used to offer or suggest something together.
usage: Use it when you plan a meeting and need a time.
leelaQ: What time do you like to meet friends?
answer: I like to meet them in the evening.

en: Do you have any plans for the Pongal holidays?
tamil: பொங்கல் விடுமுறைக்கு ஏதாவது பிளான் இருக்கா?
context: Asking a friend about festival plans.
explain: 'Do you have any plans for' is a natural way to ask about future time.
usage: Use it before a holiday to start a friendly talk.
leelaQ: What are your plans for the next holiday?
answer: I plan to visit my village.

en: Can you make it to my daughter's birthday party?
tamil: என் பொண்ணு பிறந்தநாள் பார்ட்டிக்கு வர முடியுமா?
context: Inviting a neighbour.
explain: 'Make it' means to be able to come.
usage: Use it when you invite someone and want to know if they can come.
leelaQ: Can you come to a party on a weekday?
answer: It is difficult, but I can come in the evening.

en: Where are you planning to go for your honeymoon?
tamil: தேனிலவுக்கு எங்க போகலாம்னு இருக்கீங்க?
context: Asking a newly engaged friend.
explain: 'Planning to go' asks about an intended future action.
usage: Use it to ask a friend about a coming trip with interest.
leelaQ: Where would you go for a dream holiday?
answer: I would go to Kashmir with my family.

en: How about meeting near the temple at five?
tamil: ஐந்து மணிக்கு கோயில் பக்கத்துல சந்திச்சா எப்படி?
context: Suggesting a place and time.
explain: 'How about' is followed by an -ing word to give a suggestion.
usage: Use it to suggest a place and time to a friend.
leelaQ: Where should friends meet in your town?
answer: They can meet near the bus stand.

en: Did you get my invitation for the housewarming?
tamil: புதுமனை புகுவிழாவுக்கான என் அழைப்பிதழ் உங்களுக்குக் கிடைச்சுதா?
context: Checking if a guest received the invitation.
explain: 'Did you get' asks about a past event with a result.
usage: Use it to check with a guest after you send an invitation.
leelaQ: Have you received an invitation recently?
answer: Yes, I got one for a wedding last week.

en: Will you be coming with your family?
tamil: குடும்பத்தோட வருவீங்களா?
context: Asking an invited guest.
explain: 'Will you be coming' is a gentle way to ask about future plans.
usage: Use it to know how many guests to expect.
leelaQ: Do you go to functions with your family?
answer: Yes, we all go together.

en: What are you doing after office today?
tamil: இன்னைக்கு ஆபீஸ் முடிஞ்சதும் என்ன பண்ணப்போறீங்க?
context: Asking a colleague about the evening.
explain: Present continuous with a time word asks about a plan.
usage: Use it when you want to invite a colleague for tea or a walk.
leelaQ: What do you do after office?
answer: I go home, cook and watch television.

en: Is it okay if we shift the meeting to Wednesday?
tamil: மீட்டிங்கை புதன்கிழமைக்கு மாத்தினா பரவாயில்லையா?
context: Asking a client to reschedule.
explain: 'Is it okay if' politely asks for permission to change something.
usage: Use it with clients or seniors when you need a new date.
leelaQ: How do you ask to change a meeting day?
answer: I ask if it is okay to move it to another day.

en: Have you decided where to go for the weekend?
tamil: வார இறுதிக்கு எங்க போறதுன்னு முடிவு பண்ணிட்டீங்களா?
context: Asking family about plans.
explain: 'Where to go' joins a question word with 'to' and a verb.
usage: Use it with family or friends when a plan is still open.
leelaQ: How do you decide where to go for a weekend?
answer: We talk together and choose a nearby place.

en: Why don't we go out for coffee?
tamil: காபி குடிக்க வெளியில போகலாமா?
context: Making a casual suggestion.
explain: 'Why don't we' is a friendly way to suggest something.
usage: Use it to suggest a short outing to a friend or colleague.
leelaQ: What do you like to do with friends?
answer: I like to go for coffee and chat.

en: Who else is coming to the party?
tamil: பார்ட்டிக்கு வேற யாரெல்லாம் வராங்க?
context: Asking a friend about guests.
explain: 'Who else' asks for more people besides those already known.
usage: Use it before attending an event to know the other guests.
leelaQ: Who do you like to meet at parties?
answer: I like to meet my old friends.

en: Could we reschedule our call to tomorrow morning?
tamil: நம்ம கால்-ஐ நாளைக்கு காலைக்கு மாத்தலாமா?
context: Asking a client to change the call time.
explain: 'Could we' is more polite than 'can we'.
usage: Use it at work when you cannot keep an earlier time.
leelaQ: Have you ever rescheduled a meeting?
answer: Yes, I rescheduled it because of heavy rain.

en: What should I bring for the get-together?
tamil: கூடுகைக்கு நான் என்ன கொண்டு வரணும்?
context: Asking the host what to bring.
explain: 'Should I' asks for advice or instruction.
usage: Use it to ask a host before attending a small party.
leelaQ: What do you bring when you visit someone?
answer: I bring sweets or fruits.

en: Did you enjoy the trip to Rameswaram?
tamil: ராமேஸ்வரம் டிரிப் நல்லா இருந்துச்சா?
context: Asking a colleague about their holiday.
explain: 'Did you enjoy' asks about a past experience.
usage: Use it when a friend comes back from a trip.
leelaQ: Did you enjoy your last holiday?
answer: Yes, I enjoyed it very much.

en: How long will you stay at your native place?
tamil: உங்க சொந்த ஊர்ல எவ்வளவு நாள் இருப்பீங்க?
context: Asking about someone's holiday length.
explain: 'How long' asks about the length of time.
usage: Use it to know when a colleague will be back from a break.
leelaQ: How long do you stay at your hometown?
answer: I stay for about a week.

en: Do you want to go together or meet there?
tamil: சேர்ந்து போகலாமா, இல்ல அங்க சந்திக்கலாமா?
context: Planning how to reach a function.
explain: An 'or' question offers two choices.
usage: Use it when you plan travel with a friend to an event.
leelaQ: Do you like travelling alone or with others?
answer: I like travelling with my family.

en: Is the function on a weekday or a weekend?
tamil: விசேஷம் வார நாள்லயா வார இறுதிலயா?
context: Checking the day of an event.
explain: This 'or' question asks which of two options is correct.
usage: Use it before you apply for leave or plan your travel.
leelaQ: Do you prefer functions on weekdays or weekends?
answer: I prefer weekends because I am free.

en: Can I bring my friend along?
tamil: என் நண்பனையும் கூட்டிட்டு வரலாமா?
context: Asking the host for permission.
explain: 'Bring along' means to bring with you.
usage: Use it to ask an invitation host before bringing another guest.
leelaQ: Who would you bring to a party?
answer: I would bring my close friend.

en: When are you planning to book the tickets?
tamil: டிக்கெட் எப்ப புக் பண்ணலாம்னு இருக்கீங்க?
context: Asking a friend about a trip.
explain: 'When are you planning to' asks about timing of an intended action.
usage: Use it when you are travelling together and the booking is pending.
leelaQ: When do you book tickets for a festival trip?
answer: I book them two months before.

en: What time does the programme start?
tamil: நிகழ்ச்சி எத்தனை மணிக்கு ஆரம்பிக்கும்?
context: Asking about an event timing.
explain: Present simple is used for scheduled events.
usage: Use it to confirm the time before leaving for a programme.
leelaQ: What time do your functions usually start?
answer: They usually start in the morning.

en: Shall we postpone the picnic to next Sunday?
tamil: சுற்றுலாவை அடுத்த ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமைக்குத் தள்ளி வைக்கலாமா?
context: Suggesting a delay to a group.
explain: 'Shall we' is a polite suggestion for a group.
usage: Use it when the weather or other reasons spoil a group plan.
leelaQ: When do you postpone a plan?
answer: I postpone it when it rains heavily.

en: Please send me the invitation card on WhatsApp.
tamil: அழைப்பிதழை WhatsApp-ல அனுப்புங்க, please.
context: Asking a relative for the invitation.
explain: 'Please' makes a request polite. 'Send me' is an imperative.
usage: Use it to ask for event details by message.
leelaQ: How do people send invitations these days?
answer: They send them on WhatsApp.

en: Could you please remind me about the meeting tomorrow?
tamil: நாளைக்கு மீட்டிங் இருக்கறத எனக்கு ஞாபகப்படுத்த முடியுமா?
context: Asking a colleague for a reminder.
explain: 'Could you please' is a very polite request form.
usage: Use it when you worry you may forget a plan.
leelaQ: How do you remember your appointments?
answer: I set a reminder on my phone.

en: Please keep Saturday evening free for us.
tamil: சனிக்கிழமை சாயங்காலத்தை எங்களுக்காக ஃப்ரீயா வெச்சிக்கோங்க.
context: Asking a friend to save a date.
explain: 'Keep ... free' means do not make other plans.
usage: Use it to ask a friend to be available for an event.
leelaQ: Which day do you keep free for family?
answer: I keep Sunday free for my family.

en: Can we meet a little earlier than planned?
tamil: திட்டமிட்டதை விட கொஞ்சம் சீக்கிரம் சந்திக்கலாமா?
context: Asking a friend to change the time.
explain: 'Than planned' compares the new time with the old plan.
usage: Use it when you need to change an arranged time slightly.
leelaQ: Do you like to reach early or late?
answer: I like to reach early.

en: Please come early and help us with the arrangements.
tamil: தயவு செஞ்சு சீக்கிரம் வந்து ஏற்பாடுகள்ல உதவுங்க.
context: Asking a relative to help.
explain: 'Come and help' joins two actions in one request.
usage: Use it to ask close relatives to help in a function.
leelaQ: How do you help at family functions?
answer: I help with serving food to guests.

en: Could you tell me the exact date of the wedding?
tamil: கல்யாணத்தோட சரியான தேதியைச் சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking a friend for the date.
explain: 'Could you tell me' is polite. The date part is not a question form.
usage: Use it to confirm details before applying for leave.
leelaQ: Why do we need the exact date of an event?
answer: We need it to plan our leave and travel.

en: Give me a call when you reach the hotel.
tamil: ஹோட்டலுக்குப் போனதும் எனக்கு ஒரு போன் பண்ணுங்க.
context: Asking a friend to inform you.
explain: 'Give me a call' means phone me. 'When you reach' uses present tense.
usage: Use it with family or friends who are travelling.
leelaQ: Who do you call after reaching a new place?
answer: I call my mother first.

en: Please confirm your seat by tomorrow evening.
tamil: நாளை சாயங்காலத்துக்குள்ள உங்க இடத்தை உறுதி பண்ணுங்க.
context: Asking a group member to confirm.
explain: 'By tomorrow evening' sets a deadline.
usage: Use it when you organise a trip or a group booking.
leelaQ: How do you confirm a booking?
answer: I confirm it by phone or message.

en: Can you adjust the timing a little for me?
tamil: எனக்காக நேரத்தை கொஞ்சம் மாத்திக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking a manager for a flexible time.
explain: 'Adjust' means to change a little. 'For me' shows a personal favour.
usage: Use it when you need a small favour about time.
leelaQ: When do you ask people to adjust the time?
answer: I ask when I have an urgent family work.

en: Please don't make any plans for that day.
tamil: அந்த நாளுக்கு எந்த பிளானும் போட வேண்டாம்.
context: Asking a family member to stay free.
explain: A negative imperative uses 'don't' with the base verb.
usage: Use it when a big family event falls on a certain day.
leelaQ: What do you do when a big day is coming?
answer: I plan everything and tell my family early.

en: Would you mind picking me up at the junction?
tamil: ஜங்ஷன்ல வந்து என்னைக் கூட்டிட்டுப் போக முடியுமா?
context: Asking a friend for a lift.
explain: 'Would you mind' is followed by an -ing word. It is very polite.
usage: Use it to ask a friend for help with transport.
leelaQ: Who gives you a lift when you need it?
answer: My brother gives me a lift.

en: Kindly let us know your plans by the end of this week.
tamil: இந்த வாரக் கடைசிக்குள்ள உங்க பிளானை எங்களுக்குத் தெரியப்படுத்துங்க.
context: Writing to a guest or a client.
explain: 'Kindly' is formal and polite. Use it in messages and mails.
usage: Use it in a formal message when you need an answer by a date.
leelaQ: How do you ask for a reply in a formal message?
answer: I write kindly let me know by Friday.

en: Please wait a moment, let me check my schedule.
tamil: ஒரு நிமிஷம் இருங்க, என் அட்டவணையைப் பார்க்கிறேன்.
context: Replying on the phone.
explain: 'Let me check' is a polite way to gain a little time.
usage: Use it on a call when you must check your free time.
leelaQ: What do you check before accepting a plan?
answer: I check my calendar and my work.

en: Please save me a seat near the front.
tamil: எனக்கு முன்னாடி பக்கத்துல ஒரு இடம் பிடிச்சு வைங்க.
context: Asking a friend to keep a seat at an event.
explain: 'Save me a seat' means keep a place for me.
usage: Use it when you may reach an event late.
leelaQ: Where do you like to sit in a hall?
answer: I like to sit near the front.

en: Let's keep the plan simple and not spend too much.
tamil: பிளானை எளிமையா வெச்சு அதிகம் செலவு பண்ணாம இருப்போம்.
context: Suggesting a budget plan to friends.
explain: 'Let's keep' invites everyone to follow the same idea.
usage: Use it when friends plan a trip and want to save money.
leelaQ: How do you plan a trip on a small budget?
answer: I choose a nearby place and carry home food.

en: My cousins are visiting us during the summer holidays.
tamil: கோடை விடுமுறைல என் cousins எங்களைப் பார்க்க வராங்க.
context: Telling a friend about holiday guests.
explain: Present continuous with a time phrase shows a planned visit.
usage: Use it to explain why your holidays will be busy.
leelaQ: Who visits you during the holidays?
answer: My cousins visit us every summer.

en: I'll message you the location once everyone confirms.
tamil: எல்லாரும் உறுதி பண்ணினதும் இடத்தை மெசேஜ் பண்றேன்.
context: Organising a small gathering.
explain: 'Once' links the two actions in time. The 'once' part uses present tense.
usage: Use it as the organiser of a group plan.
leelaQ: How do you share a place with friends?
answer: I send the location on WhatsApp.

en: We have a family function every year in January.
tamil: ஒவ்வொரு வருஷமும் ஜனவரில எங்களுக்கு ஒரு குடும்ப விழா இருக்கும்.
context: Describing a yearly tradition.
explain: Present simple with 'every year' shows a regular event.
usage: Use it to explain a tradition to a new friend or colleague.
leelaQ: Which yearly event do you enjoy most?
answer: I enjoy Pongal the most.

en: Did you plan anything special for your anniversary?
tamil: உங்க திருமண நாளுக்கு ஏதாவது சிறப்பா பிளான் பண்ணீங்களா?
context: Asking a colleague about a celebration.
explain: 'Anything special' asks if there is something different from normal.
usage: Use it to show interest in a colleague's celebration.
leelaQ: How do you celebrate special days?
answer: We go out for dinner as a family.

en: Please tell the others that the plan has changed.
tamil: பிளான் மாறிடுச்சுன்னு மத்தவங்ககிட்ட சொல்லுங்க.
context: Asking a friend to spread information.
explain: 'Has changed' shows the result is true now.
usage: Use it when a group plan changes and you cannot call everyone.
leelaQ: How do you inform a group about a change?
answer: I send a message in the group chat.

en: I don't think we can finish shopping before the function.
tamil: விசேஷத்துக்கு முன்னாடி ஷாப்பிங் முடிக்க முடியும்னு தோணல.
context: Worrying about time with family.
explain: 'I don't think' softens a negative opinion.
usage: Use it when you are worried about time before an event.
leelaQ: Do you finish shopping early or late?
answer: I finish it early to avoid the crowd.
